text:
maria: quick sync — need clarification on per-route quota behavior for the billing change. If a route's bucket is exhausted but the system can serve from global/burst capacity, what does the endpoint return (429 vs success)? also what headers/body should clients rely on? trying to avoid SDK churn.

alex: short answer: avoid returning 200 silently if quota was exceeded — better to signal. but we can surface that it was served from fallback.

maria: by "signal" do you mean 429 then retry-from-fallback? that would break UX. we need a contract.

alex: right. proposal: two behaviors depending on policy
- if policy == "reject-on-route-exhaust": return 429 (throttle). include Retry-After and quota headers.
- if policy == "serve-from-fallback": return 200 but include explicit headers so clients know it used fallback/burst capacity. clients can opt-in to treat that as degraded.

maria: example headers? need to be stable names (avoid renaming X-RateLimit-* right away).

luca: runtime note — we already emit internal bucket ids. suggested header set (backcompat + new):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 10
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1680000000
X-RW-Quota-Bucket: route:GET:/v1/generate:abc123
X-RW-Quota-Policy: reject-on-route-exhaust
X-RW-Quota-Info: fallback=false
```
and for served-from-fallback:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RW-Quota-Bucket: route:GET:/v1/generate:abc123
X-RW-Quota-Policy: serve-from-fallback
X-RW-Quota-Info: fallback=true;source=global-pool
X-RW-Quota-Remaining: 0
```
Note: keep X-RateLimit-* while we migrate clients, but new X-RW-* is the authoritative shape.

tanya: product question — how long do we keep the old headers? SDKs will read X-RateLimit-Remaining. deprecate timeline?

alex: recommend 6 months of dual writing, then emit a WARN in logs + docs for 3 months, then deprecate. also publish a compatibility page.

jon: ops: need to define fallback semantics for canary rollout. when we flip the flag we should:
1) enable fallback in canary (10% traffic)
2) monitor success/error + tail latency + cost delta
3) if errors spike, auto revert to reject-on-route-exhaust for canary
this avoids surprising downstream clients.

ryan: on-call note — clients often retry aggressively on 429. if we return 200 with fallback but keep X-RW-Quota-Info:fallback=true, many SDKs will ignore it. Can we also emit a top-level Warning header so intermediaries see degraded handling?

luca: we can add `Warning: 299 "served-from-fallback"` and a metric tag. good call.

maria: sounds good. doc checklist for engineering:
- spec PR with header shapes and examples (include both 429 and fallback 200)
- SDK owners notified and sample code for detecting fallback (use X-RW-Quota-Info or Warning)
- rollout plan (jon + luca) + canary thresholds
- deprecation timeline for old headers (alex + tanya)

tanya: i'll own the docs + comms. can someone draft the PR? @alex? :+1:

alex: i'll draft the spec PR today. will include examples and a migration guide for SDKs.

jon: i'll add the rollout playbook and canary config.

ryan: i'll add a note to oncall runbook about interpreting 200+fallback vs 429. also suggest default client backoff guidance: exponential with jitter, cap 60s.

maria: perfect. last Q — response body for 429, should it include machine-readable reason? we have some clients that parse JSON error codes.

alex: yes, include a stable error code field in JSON error body, e.g.:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limited",
    "code": "quota_route_exhausted",
    "message": "per-route quota exhausted for route GET /v1/generate",
    "retry_after": 10
  }
}
```
For fallback-served 200 responses we should NOT include an error body — use headers + Warning.

maria: awesome. @tanya i'll ping you for the comms draft after alex's PR. thanks all :rocket:

deploy-bot: deploy queued — canary config updated for quota-fallback feature (deploy id: dpl_20240312_42)

jon: noted. we'll watch the canary dashboard and loop back in ~24h.

ryan: adding a one-liner to the runbook now.

alex: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/r/rw/infrapkg/-/merge_requests/1234 — includes header examples and SDK migration notes.

maria: closing the loop. will post final doc link once tanya and alex finish. thanks everyone!
